What Is Bybit TradFi? Bybit TradFi is a dedicated section on the Bybit App and website designed to make traditional market access easier to find, understand, and trade. It brings two products together under one category: TradFi Perpetuals and CFD. Together, they give users access to selected traditional market exposure across forex, metals, indices, stocks, and commodities, while keeping the experience connected to the Bybit ecosystem. A Clearer Product Structure As part of the July 2026 update, the product previously known as “TradFi” has been renamed CFD. For existing users, the core trading experience remains unchanged. Instruments, leverage, fee structures, available funds, and open positions remain the same. The update mainly improves how TradFi products are organized, making it easier for users to understand which product fits their trading style. TradFi Perpetuals TradFi Perpetuals are designed for users who want traditional market exposure through a familiar Bybit-native experience. They trade 24/7, settle in USDT, and can be accessed through the Unified Trading Account. No MT5 download or separate account setup is required. This makes TradFi Perpetuals suitable for users who want simpler access to selected traditional markets using the same infrastructure they already use on Bybit. CFD CFD is designed for users who want broader instrument coverage and more advanced trading tools. It provides access to 400+ instruments and is available through MetaTrader 5, Bybit App, and Bybit Web. It also supports advanced charting, Expert Advisors, and leverage of up to 500x on selected forex pairs. CFD uses a dedicated MT5 CFD Account, separate from the Unified Trading Account. Choosing the Right Product TradFi Perpetuals are best suited for users who want 24/7 access, USDT settlement, and a simple Bybit-native experience. CFD is better suited for users who want MT5 tools, a wider range of instruments, and more advanced trading functionality. The Bottom Line Bybit TradFi gives users a clearer way to access selected traditional markets from one platform. TradFi Perpetuals offer simplicity and 24/7 access. CFD offers broader coverage and advanced tools. The result is a more organized bridge between digital asset trading and traditional market exposure. With the November midterm elections approaching, one theme runs through nearly every asset class: the deficit problem isn’t going away, regardless of which party emerges on top. In Jan van Eck’s Q3 2026 Investment Outlook, he said that investors should stay invested but be increasingly selective. Our investment teams broadly echoed this view, as they focus on the policy and market dynamics the election results may set in motion. To help investors understand the potential impact across asset classes, we asked investment team leaders two questions: What election issues and market indicators should investors be watching in relation to your asset class/strategy? What do you view as the biggest risks and opportunities in your space through the end of 2026? Read on to see how the 2026 Midterm Elections may impact: Gold Commodities Fixed Income Municipal Bonds Emerging Markets Bonds Emerging Markets Equity Digital Assets Private Markets Should the 2026 Midterm Elections Drive Major Shifts in Gold Allocations? Fiscal Pressure Keeps Gold Case Intact Ima Casanova | Portfolio Manager, Gold and Precious Metals Indicators to Watch We believe gold investors should focus less on the election result itself than on the policy path and market reaction that follow. Continued Republican control could mean greater continuity in the current policy environment, while a shift to divided government could introduce greater legislative gridlock, oversight and political uncertainty. In either case, the implications for the U.S. dollar, interest rates and fiscal policy are likely to matter more for gold than the party outcome itself. The 2014 midterms offer one example: Republicans gained control of the Senate and expanded their House majority, while the immediate market reaction included a stronger U.S. dollar and sharp weakness in gold. Brooke Unger

Senior digital editor



 Time was when Manchester United was the football club that English non-supporters tended to despise. But that sentiment is pallid compared with the anger now directed at Manchester City, which broke spending rules to become England’s most successful team, an independent commission alleges. 
 
https://click.e.economist.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMTZ9AAcAAAAAB0rEMbZuKuurLTAd53okHw_6vmAwRH6wZ9HjlXZB0UXupITsN8fyGyM5cTXuA4rkzUBK9gzZdIbpsburvxxVr_ZiErVmzccYewhsfOMP
